messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: High 95th-percentile latency observed in generation-api (region: us-west-2). Pager INC-1817643210 created at 1817643210. Severity: P2. Please ACK and start triage. 

Anya Patel: Acked. I'm on it — picking up triage. Quick context: customers report slow responses and occasional 503s. No page of error spikes, mostly tail latency.

Mike Chen: Thanks Anya. First quick things: 1) check replica health `kubectl get deploy generation-api -n prod -o wide` 2) check queue length on request-proxy: `redis-cli -n 3 LLEN rq:gen` 3) tail recent logs: `stern generation-api -n prod --since 15m`

Anya Patel: Ran commands: replicas=3, CPU usage high on pod generation-api-2, queue length at 120, and a bunch of 429/503 from model-host-v2. Pushing immediate mitigation: increase burst scaling to 5, and temporarily route non-critical low-cost traffic to model-host-v1 fallback.

Sanjay Rao: Good call. Customer impact: hosted text-generation and streaming endpoints may see elevated latency; embeddings unaffected. We should post a brief status page entry and trigger CS notification for accounts with active SLAs.

Julie Carter: Draft cust-facing ack (for Zendesk/Intercom):

```
Hi — thanks for the report. We’re currently investigating elevated latency on the Redwood generation API affecting some text-generation requests. Our on-call team is working on mitigation. We’ll post updates here and on status.redwood.ai. No action needed from you right now.
Estimated next update: ~20 minutes.
ID: INC-1817643210
```

Julie Carter: Can we get an internal short-form update for the CS escalation channel so support agents can triage incoming tickets?

Anya Patel: Internal CS snippet: 

"Incident INC-1817643210 — Elevated generation-api latency. On-call implemented horizontal scale and traffic fallback to model-host-v1. Customers may see slower responses or transient 503s. SRE estimating mitigation in ~15-30m. For SLA accounts, escalate to Julie.Carter. Do not escalate to legal yet"

Mike Chen: Also adding runbook steps I'm executing now: 
1) `kubectl scale deploy generation-api --replicas=5 -n prod`
2) `redwood-cli route set --service generation-api --fallback model-host-v1 --region us-west-2`
3) increase request proxy workers: `systemctl restart redwood-request-proxy` on the two machines with highest CPU
4) check model-host-v2 GPU memory: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv`

Anya Patel: Executed 1 and 2. Scale succeeded; fallback routing applied. Queue drained from 120 -> 40 in ~3m. Latency 95th dropped from 1.4s -> 860ms but still above SLO. Continuing investigation into model-host-v2 kernel OOMs.

Sanjay Rao: Prepare status page entry. Keep it concise and non-technical. Suggested text: 

"We are investigating elevated latency for our text generation API in US-West. Some customers may experience slower responses or transient errors. Our team has applied mitigation and is monitoring. Updates every 20 minutes. ID: INC-1817643210."

Anya Patel: Posting that now to status.redwood.ai (internal note: we use the quick-update template).

Zendesk Bot: Suggested macros for support agents found in library: title: "INC-1817643210 - Customer acknowledgment". Do you want to push new macro?

Julie Carter: Please push the new macro. Template we want saved (short):

Initial ACK macro:

"Hi {{customer.first_name}},
Thanks for contacting Redwood. We’re aware of an incident affecting text-generation latency (INC-1817643210). Our engineers are actively working on mitigation. We’ll update you by {{eta}}. — Julia, Redwood Support"

Update macro (20m):

"Update on INC-1817643210: mitigation in progress. We’ve scaled services and applied a temporary fallback to maintain availability. You may see improved response times; we’ll follow up when we have a root cause. — Redwood Support"

Resolution macro:

"INC-1817643210 resolved: Services restored to normal performance, and fallback removed. If you still see issues, please reply and include request IDs. Thank you for your patience."

Julie Carter: Also adding an internal troubleshooting checklist for L1 agents to triage tickets before escalation: 
- Confirm customer endpoint and timestamp
- Ask for request ID(s) and sample request payload
- Confirm if issue persists after 5–10 minutes
- If ticket is SLA-critical, tag with priority=high and notify Julie Carter directly

Anya Patel: Leaving a handoff note for next oncall (ops shift change in 25m): 
"Handoff: INC-1817643210 — mitigation applied: scaled to 5 replicas, fallback to model-host-v1 enabled, queue draining. Current 95p latency ~850ms. Working hypothesis: model-host-v2 memory pressure causing throttling. Next steps: inspect model-host-v2 pod logs for OOMs, check recent model rollout (deploy tag v2.3.1 rolled 2h ago)."

Ops Lead: Thanks Anya. Take a break if you need. Next oncall (Sanjay) — please pick up in 25m. Add the following to the post-mortem TODOs: investigate rollout timing, consider reverting v2.3.1 to v2.3.0 if repeatable.

Sanjay Rao: Got it. I'll join in 20m and run full model-host diag. I'll also coordinate a brief customer follow-up if we see resolution sooner. :thumbsup:

Anya Patel: Quick notes to paste into the incident timeline for the postmortem: 
- 1817643210 alert triggered.
- 1817643240 Anya ack + runbook start.
- 1817643305 scaled replicas + applied fallback.
- 1817643360 queue drained and partial latency improvement.
- 1817643520 still under observation, handed off to Sanjay at 1817643540.

Julie Carter: Thanks team. I'll push macros and CS snippet now and watch incoming tickets. Ping me in #support-escalations for urgent SLA cases.

oncall-bot: REMINDER: Shift handoff scheduled at 1817643550. Please ensure handoff notes are in the thread.

Mike Chen: Leaving one more small debug snippet for engineers: 

```bash
# quickly see recent OOMs on model-host-v2 nodes
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l model-host=v2 -o name); do kubectl describe $n | grep -i oom -A2 || true; done
```

Ops Lead: Good run. Keep monitoring, and we’ll assemble the postmortem template once this is stable. :wave:
